content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, they all appear to be from July 2024 (dates 2024-07-16 through 2024-07-19) except for one on 2024-12-02. Let me examine the patterns.

## Example 1 (2024-07-17)
- History: Price range ~66-71, generally stable
- Sentiment: Mix of positive (0.67, 1.00), neutral (0.33), and negative (-0.33)
- Model forecasts: Start around 66.34, gradually increasing to ~70 by day 12
- True outcomes: Start around 66.42, but by day 12 we see 71.17 (model predicted 70.56)

The model appears to be under-predicting the price increases, especially after day 12.

## Example 2 (2024-07-18)
- Very similar to Example 1
- Model forecasts start at 66.13
- True outcomes exceed predictions, especially the 71.17 on day 12 vs 70.45 predicted

## Example 3 (2024-07-16)
- Model forecasts start at 67.63
- True outcomes: 67.94 on day 1 (model was low)
- Again, predictions are too low, especially after day 10-12

## Example 4 (2024-07-19)
- Model forecasts: [66.27, 65.29, 66.35, 69.60, ...]
- True outcomes: [66.00, 64.79, 65.79, 68.90, ...]

Wait, looking at this more carefully:
- Day 1: Model 66.27 vs True 66.00 (model +0.27 high)


- Day 2: Model 65.29 vs True 64.79 (model +0.50 high)
- Day 3: Model 66.35 vs True 65.79 (model +0.56 high)
- Day 4: Model 69.60 vs True 68.90 (model +0.70 high)
- Days 5-9: Model matches true outcomes closely
